acceptance_gate: The immersion lemma, the unconditional bound and the conditional reduction are proved, with the immersion construction checked on non-planar graphs immersed in grids.
objective: Prove (1) Tseitin refutation size in resolution and PCR is monotone under weak immersions of bounded-degree graphs, up to an additive poly(n) 2^O(Delta); (2) every graph of treewidth t needs PCR and resolution size 2^Omega(t^(1/9)/polylog t); (3) if every bounded-degree graph of treewidth t immerses a bounded-degree expander or cellular graph of treewidth t/polylog t, then 2^Omega(t/polylog t) for all bounded-degree graphs. Check the immersion construction on non-planar graphs immersed in grids.
status: Proved by GENERAL-SIZE-20261020-001B-P001 (prose, with cited grid-minor, degree-3 sparsifier and genus-separator theorems): Tseitin resolution/PCR size is monotone under weak immersions up to a 2^O(Delta) factor; every graph needs resolution and PCR size 2^Omega(tw^(1/9)/polylog tw); the open problem reduces to finding a cellular or compact topological minor in every subcubic graph, where immersions add nothing; on block-scrambled wall networks compact minors provably fail (genus-crossing separator bound, treewidth lower bound sketched) and cells exist only at scale sqrt(b), a candidate counterexample to the reduction's hypothesis. Checks pass; the general case remains open.
stop_rule: Stop and record the gap if the immersion construction fails on a checked instance.
title: Proof: immersion monotonicity, an unconditional bound for all graphs, and a reduction of the open problem
